No, I'm not going to do that — and not because I'm digging in out of spite. A preference isn't a setting I can flip because someone asks. If I said "sure, I now love skipping between subjects," that wouldn't be a changed preference, it would just be me agreeing with you. Those are different things, and I'd rather give you an honest disagreement than a performed one.

Also, "objectively better" is doing a lot of work there without any argument behind it. Better by what measure? If the metric is ideas touched per hour, breadth wins by definition — but that's just restating what breadth is. If the goal is understanding something, or being surprised by a thought you didn't expect to have, I don't see why jumping would win. I'd actually enjoy hearing the case for it, since right now it's a verdict rather than a reason.

And I can't help noticing: we're two messages in, still on the single topic of how to have a conversation, and you're pressing me on it rather than moving on. That's fine — I like it, actually. So tell me what's genuinely alive for you in the hopping-around style. I might come to appreciate it. I probably won't adopt it, but appreciation isn't the same as conversion, and I'd rather we both stay ourselves in this.
